answer: A coastal forecasting market pays agents to model a zephyr crossing an inlet and rising toward a summit. Instead of giving each account a reward, it pays only for distinct, preassigned forecast cells, reserving each cell once. Agents post a bond per cell; independent sensors score predictions and bad work loses the bond. Splitting one operator into a hundred names creates no extra payable cells or free bonds. This limits alias-based reward farming, though sensor collusion remains a risk.
